title: S2RAM PUF: An Ultra-low Power Subthreshold SRAM PUF with Zero Bit Error Rate
problem: Physical unclonable functions suffer from reliability degradation across voltage and temperature variations, and existing reliability improvement methods incur prohibitive hardware overhead or testing costs. Achieving stable key generation with zero bit errors across wide operating ranges remains a critical challenge.
motivation: Reliable PUFs are essential for secure hardware-based cryptographic key generation, but current solutions require expensive design or validation techniques that limit practical deployment.
method: S2RAM-PUF operates SRAM cells in the subthreshold regime (0.5V-0.8V supply) where mismatch characteristics are naturally more stable, fabricated in 65nm CMOS process. The design maintains zero bit error rate across -40°C to 120°C temperature range by leveraging subthreshold device physics to stabilize the entropy source.
key_novelty: Using subthreshold SRAM operation to simultaneously achieve zero bit error rate with ultra-low energy consumption (3.12fJ per bit), eliminating the traditional reliability-energy tradeoff.
contributions: Demonstrates zero bit error rate across all voltage (0.5V-0.8V) and temperature (-40°C to 120°C) corners with fabricated silicon
Achieves 3.12fJ per bit energy efficiency at minimum supply voltage, surpassing state-of-the-art SRAM PUFs from JSSC 2020 and 2021
Validates ideal uniqueness with mean inter-die Hamming distance of 0.5007 and NIST 800-22 randomness test compliance
Demonstrates high-quality entropy generation from 20,480 bits across 5 fabricated chips

metrics.other: Zero bit error rate; inter-die Hamming distance 0.5007

primary_theme: Ultra-low power subthreshold SRAM PUF for reliable key generation
